title: Deck Staining in Williston, FL | Strip, Sand & Seal
description: Deck staining in Williston, FL: strip, sand, replace soft boards, and apply penetrating stain that is back-brushed into the wood. Free written estimate.
heroIntro: We restore Williston decks by getting down to clean wood and then working the stain in. The walking surface gets the most attention because it takes the most abuse.

questions: How often should a deck be stained in Florida?
Should I use transparent or solid stain on my deck?
Do you replace rotten deck boards?

sections.h2: Horizontal wood takes the hardest hit
body: A wall sheds rain. A deck holds it in every fastener hole and board gap, then bakes in direct sun until the surface checks and cups. That is why deck staining in Williston, FL wears out faster than the paint on the house next to it. On acreage properties, decks and porches also collect dust and grit that grind into the finish.
If your boards feel soft or spongy, read our article on signs of deck wood rot before deciding on a stain.

sections.h2: Getting back to bare, sound wood
body: We wash and strip the old coating, then sand the walking surface so the new stain soaks in evenly. Proud fasteners get set, loose hardware is fixed, and boards that probe soft are replaced. Railings and stairs get the same treatment, since hands and feet wear them in different ways.

bullets: Transparent: shows the most grain, needs recoating sooner
Semi-transparent: a balance of grain and UV protection
Solid: hides variation in older or mismatched boards, protects longest against sun
body: We use penetrating stains on exposed wood, sprayed and then back-brushed so the product gets into the grain rather than sitting on top. The exact product is named on your estimate.

sections.h2: Decks in town and decks on acreage
body: A deck behind a house in Williston Highlands usually gets weekend foot traffic and grill grease. A wraparound porch on a farm property sees boots, feed dust, and much more sun because there are fewer trees around it. The prep is the same in principle, but the second one often needs more sanding and a more opaque stain to hold up.
Whichever you have, a crew lead looks at board condition, fasteners, and how the deck drains before recommending a product. Find our other services for the town on the Williston painters page.

Wood needs to be dry before stain goes on, so Williston deck work fits best into the October through May stretch. Summer jobs are possible with early starts and close attention to the forecast. If your fence needs attention too, fence staining in Williston can be done in the same mobilization. Our main deck and fence staining service has more on stain types.

faqs.q: How often does a Williston deck need restaining?
faqs.a: It depends on sun exposure, foot traffic, and stain opacity. Transparent finishes need attention sooner than solid ones. We can assess your deck during a free walkthrough.
Yes. Boards that probe soft are replaced during prep, and we fix loose hardware and set raised fasteners.

faqs.q: Can you stain my porch and deck together?
faqs.a: Yes. Porches, stairs, and railings can all be included on one estimate with the same stain system.

faqs.q: Do you sand the deck or just wash it?
faqs.a: We sand the walking surface after washing and stripping, so the new stain absorbs evenly instead of blotching over old coating.
